:::{#exm-dot-product-inner-product}
#### The dot product is an inner product

The dot product (@def-dot-product) is an inner product on $\reals^p$,
called the **Euclidean** or **standard** inner product.
Each of the four properties in @def-inner-product holds:

- **positivity**: $\vx \cdot \vx = \sumip x_i^2$
  is a sum of squares, so it is at least $0$;
- **definiteness**: a sum of squares is $0$ exactly when every term is $0$,
  so $\vx \cdot \vx = 0$ exactly when every $x_i = 0$,
  that is, when $\vx = \vzero_{p \times 1}$;
- **linearity in the first slot**: this property is the first-slot half of @thm-dot-linear;
- **symmetry**: this property is @thm-lincom-symmetric.

For instance, with $\vx = (1, -2, 2)$,

$$
\ba
\vx \cdot \vx
&= 1 \cd 1 + (-2) \cd (-2) + 2 \cd 2
&& \text{(definition of the dot product)}
\\
&= 1 + 4 + 4
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= 9
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

which is positive, as positivity and definiteness require of a nonzero vector.

:::
